newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine spring sowing aims at bigger grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine spring sowing aims at bigger grain harvest.

text.p: Ukraine has begun its spring sowing campaign and aims to raise its total 1997 grain harvest to 38 million tonnes from last year's 25.4 million tonnes, a senior Agriculture Ministry official said on Thursday.
Valentyn Tymoshenko, deputy head of the ministry's crop department, said Ukraine had sown 76,100 hectares to early spring grains compared to 6,600 hectares at this time last year.
The ministry planned to sow 6.10 million hectares with early spring grains, above 5.24 million hectares in 1996, he said.
Ukraine expects a wheat harvest of about 17-18 million tonnes compared to 1996's 13.4 million tonnes, Tymoshenko said. Farmers harvested 16.4 million tonnes of winter wheat in 1995.
The ministry planned to sow 4.6 million hectares with different types of corn compared to 4.5 million hectares last year.
The ministry's plan calls for sowing 1.83 million hectares with sunflower compared to 1.75 million hectares in 1996.
Ukraine also plans to sow about 1.35 million hectares to sugar beet from 1.418 million hectares sown and 24 million tonnes of sugar beet harvested last year.
Tymoshenko confirmed earlier reports that Ukraine would resow about 500,000 hectares of frost-damaged winter crops mostly in central and nothern Ukraine, out of 7.53 million hectares.
He said 6.63 million hectares had been sown to winter wheat, about 700,000 hectares to winter rye and 200,000 hectares to winter barley.

Acting Agriculture Minister Boris Supikhanov told parliament earlier this week that most of the winter wheat crop was doing better than last year and about 90 percent of fields were in good condition.
Supikhanov said there was enough seed for spring sowing and the government was storing up fuel supplies.
Tymoshenko added that Ukraine had prepared more fertiliser and pesticides for this year's harvest than in 1996.

The ministry said state and private farmers needed three billion hryvnias for spring sowing and that the government would advance 1.1-1.2 billion hryvnias in direct credits. The money would finance production and purchases of the 5.88 million tonnes of grain that the state plans to buy from the 1997 crop, it said.
